name: Hanau
summary: Wrede, whose Bavarians had changed sides a fortnight before, marched with Austrians and Bavarians to stand across Napoleon's road home at Hanau, with the Kinzig at his back and the Lamboy forest in front. On the 30th Charpentier's and Dubreton's divisions cleared the forest in skirmish order; Drouot then brought fifty of the Guard's guns out on Wrede's left and silenced his batteries, and Nansouty's Guard cavalry and Sébastiani's squadrons rode down the allied horse. Wrede's line fell back over the Kinzig, many men drowning at the Lamboy bridge, and on the 31st the Grande Armée's remnant marched on through Hanau to the Rhine.

forces.name: Charpentier's Division
forces.summary: Macdonald's leading division, which went into the Lamboy forest in skirmish order on the morning of the 30th and pushed Wrede's light troops back through the trees, opening the way for the Guard's guns.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for Hanau, from Mir's history of the battle; the page names regiments and battalions but no batteries.

Only these divisions of Victor's and Macdonald's corps were engaged, and after Leipzig their battalions were far below strength; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit many of them.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Dubreton's Division
forces.summary: Victor's division, which fought through the forest beside Charpentier's and cleared it in front of the allied centre by midday.

forces.name: The Old Guard, with Drouot's Guns
forces.formation: 1st and 2nd Old Guard Divisions (Friant, Curial), Imperial Guard
forces.summary: The Guard's infantry, which held the edge of the forest while Drouot brought its artillery out on a track towards Wrede's left. Fifty guns, massed under the Guard's protection, silenced the allied batteries and opened the way for the Guard cavalry; on the 31st the Guard marched on through Hanau.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1813.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for Hanau, from Mir's history of the battle; the page names regiments and battalions but no batteries.
The 1st Chasseurs and Grenadiers à Pied are the list's Old Guard, and the 2nd, raised in 1811, its Middle Guard.

The Fusilier regiments of Curial's division, without the Young Guard regiment the list's brigade wants beside them, show as a historical departure; the Vélites of Turin and Florence are the list's Italian brigade.

The order of battle gives the Guard artillery as forty foot and twelve horse guns, about five foot and two horse batteries. Two Old Guard foot batteries, one with each Old Guard brigade, the 12-pdr battery and the two horse batteries are here; the batteries themselves aren't named.
Drouot commanded the Guard infantry and artillery at Hanau; Friant leads the force, as its senior division commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: Two more Guard foot batteries
missing.reason: The rest of Drouot's forty foot guns, more than the list's Old Guard brigades and reserve take.

forces.name: Nansouty's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: Brought out beside Drouot's guns on Wrede's left, it fell on the Bavarian and Austrian cavalry there, the Grenadiers à Cheval and Dragoons riding them down, and drove them back on the Kinzig.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1813.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for Hanau, from Mir's history of the battle; the page names regiments and battalions but no batteries.
Each Guard regiment is shown as one unit, its Old and Young Guard squadrons together: Walther's Old Guard squadrons and Lefebvre-Desnouettes's Young Guard ones.
The Guard Cavalry's four horse batteries are from Nafziger's return of 15 October.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: Young Guard Dragoons (Pinteville)

forces.name: Sébastiani's Cavalry
forces.summary: About three thousand horsemen in twenty-two regiments, which came out with the Guard cavalry on Wrede's left and joined in the charges that drove the allied horse back.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for Hanau, from Mir's history of the battle; the page names regiments and battalions but no batteries.
The corps' twenty-two regiments had two to four squadrons each, about 140 men on average; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
The chevau-légers lanciers are the list's Lancers.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Beckers's Division
forces.summary: Part of Wrede's centre, posted along the Frankfurt road where it left the Lamboy forest. Its light troops were driven back out of the trees by Charpentier's and Dubreton's skirmishers, and when the French guns came into action its line was pounded and fell back on the Kinzig.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813; Bavaria had changed sides a fortnight before.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Hanau, from the Bavarian war archives' history.
The Kreis battalions were national field battalions, raised in 1813 from the districts' militia and often made up of parts of two; they are shown as Line.
The Wurst batteries, light 6-pdrs with the gunners riding on the limbers, are the list's Light Artillery.
The corps' artillery reserve, two 12-pdr batteries under Ulmer, is shown one with each division, as the list's Heavy Foot Battery.
The Wurst battery rides with Elbracht's chevau-légers, as the list takes a light battery in a cavalry brigade; the 3rd Chevau-légers had three squadrons.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lamotte's Division
forces.summary: Wrede's right, by the Kinzig and the Lamboy bridge. When the centre gave way it was left with the river at its back and a single bridge to cross; many men were drowned trying to get over, and the division fell back into Hanau.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813; Bavaria had changed sides a fortnight before.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Hanau, from the Bavarian war archives' history.
The Kreis battalions were national field battalions, raised in 1813 from the districts' militia and often made up of parts of two; they are shown as Line.
The Wurst batteries, light 6-pdrs with the gunners riding on the limbers, are the list's Light Artillery.
Both brigades were made up of single battalions of different regiments, so Stockh's has three regiments and Deroy's four, where the list's brigade takes two; these show as historical departures.
The corps' artillery reserve, two 12-pdr batteries under Ulmer, is shown one with each division, as the list's Heavy Foot Battery.
The Wurst battery rides with Diez's chevau-légers, as the list takes a light battery in a cavalry brigade; both regiments had three squadrons.

notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813; Bavaria had changed sides a fortnight before.

forces.name: Fresnel's Light Division
forces.summary: The Austrian light troops, Jäger, hussars and uhlans, out in front of the allied line and in the forest, the first to meet the French columns on the morning of the 30th.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Hanau, from the Bavarian war archives' history.
The division's Szekler Grenz regiment was detached to Bach's division, and is shown there.
With no line infantry brigade, which the list wants first, the division shows a historical departure. Play it alongside Bach's division.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bach's Division
forces.summary: The Austrian line infantry, with the Szekler Grenzers lent from the light division, in the allied centre beside the Bavarians; it held its ground until the French guns and cavalry broke the left, then fell back over the Kinzig.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Hanau, from the Bavarian war archives' history.

Each regiment fought with four battalions, where the list takes two Large ones; the Grenz battalions and two brigade batteries together are more additional troops than the brigade takes. These show as historical departures.

One of the corps' three 12-pdr batteries is here as the list's Position Battery; with eight line battalions, where the list wants nine for it, and one brigade where the list wants one per 500 points, these show as historical departures.

forces.name: Trautenberg's Grenadiers

forces.name: Mensdorff's Cossacks
forces.summary: Two Don Cossack regiments of Mensdorff's raiding column, which had come to join Wrede and harried the French columns on the road from Gelnhausen.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Hanau, from the Bavarian war archives' history.
Mensdorff was an Austrian officer leading a column of Russian Cossacks.
Chernyshev's and Orlov-Denisov's raiding columns, which Nafziger lists with Wrede's army, were not in the battle.
A Cossack brigade on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list wants, so this shows as a historical departure.
